fields.name: allowSubmitApprove

(admin-guides/refine-the-rules-allow-submission-despite-tolerance-9b96d467.md). configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md documents it on BOTH the Rules tab (step 6) and the Life to Date tab (step 10), so it is not Rules-tab-exclusive. Corpus enumerates only the selected state ('Select this check box to allow submission') - the cleared state is NOT documented, so no validValues are asserted.

fields.label: Exception Message

Only scattered example members appear across topics (Unit Price, Shipping, Quantity, Line Quantity, Receipt Associated, Remit Address, Request Total, Custom field). validValues deliberately left empty - a partial list would be worse than none. Value = an absolute number at or above which an exception fires; Percentage = a percent above which a flag fires. amounts-and-tolerances-ab795b1f.md corroborates the pair generically: 'this can be refined by including tolerance levels applying to the absolute currency value, or to a percentage', and states multiple rules can run on the same field. refine-the-rules-combine-the-life-to-date-and-rules-rule-types-2b46973f.md documents a tolerance value of zero as legitimate. Appears on the Rules tab, the Life to Date tab, and inside Overage Tolerance.

fields.name: toleranceCurrency
fields.label: Currency

fields.name: overageTolerance

fields.name: lifeToDateRuleType
fields.label: Life to Date
fields.sourceQuote: Click the Life to Date tab, then select the check box next to the rule type to activate using the table below:
fields.notes: LONG CATALOG, complete, in source order, from the 6-row INDENTED markdown table (grep -c '^| ' returns 0 on this file; grep -cP '^\s*\|' returns 22). Multi-select: 'Repeat by selecting a check box for each option you want to include.' Each selection reveals its own tolerance refinement. fields.name: matchAgainstReceivedQuantity

fields.name: ruleSetName
fields.label: Rule Set Name
fields.sourceQuote: Rule Set Name: The name of the rule set.

fields.name: inUse
fields.label: In Use
fields.sourceQuote: In Use: Shows if the matching rule set has been applied against any active invoice (Yes) or has not yet applied (No) in the system.
fields.notes: READ-ONLY status column, not an editable control - emitted because it is the hard gate on every write to this page: 'A rule set with an In Use status of Yes cannot be modified in any way.' Yes/No are BOTH explicitly enumerated in the cited sentence, so this is not an invented toggle pair. Clearing it requires breaking every invoice association (see the unlockRuleSet dependency).

fields.name: associatedPolicies
fields.label: Associated Policies
fields.sourceQuote: Associated Policies: Shows what Invoice PO policy has been configured to include this PO matching rule set.
fields.notes: READ-ONLY column. The association is NOT made here - it is made on the already-built Policies page via the PO Matching Ruleset option. Never re-home that field. PO Matching Rule Sets (including Receipt Confirmation outcomes) can differ per policy.

fields.name: namedRulesGroupName
fields.label: Name
fields.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Rules, type a descriptive name for the new rule in Name.
fields.notes: Names a Named Rules Group inside the rule set. Glossary definition: 'Named Rules Group: Any rule existing within ("under") the Matching Rule Set, for example, a condition-based rule group.' A shipped group called Default exists and is the documented basis for new groups.

fields.name: ruleGroupConditions
fields.label: Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions
fields.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions, configure the conditions that the system will detect and then execute the matching rule set on
fields.notes: ONLY attestation of this dialog. Reached from the page via: select rule set > Edit > select named rule group > Add. Conditions are added with Insert and committed with Save; then select the new condition > Edit Rules > (build rule) > Update > Save. Adding condition groups under a group is what makes the set a 'Multiple Matching Rule Set'. Condition-based rules run as subsets of the parent rule; if no condition is met the default rules run. Tools-guides corroborates the concept: 'Match Rules are configurable, similar to Audit and Workflow rules and can include condition-based rule groups within the overall matching rule set.' The condition operand catalog is NOT documented for this dialog - do NOT borrow the Audit Rules Condition page catalog, which is a different page already in the graph.

fields.name: confirmationType

fields.notes: Set through Edit Confirmation, which opens the Select Confirmation Type window; assignable at the Rule Set level or at an individual rule-condition level, with 'Parent choice' displayed for rule conditions to inherit the Rule Set's choice. GATE: unless the PO line's Is Receipt Required is Yes, none of this logic is evaluated at all.

fields.name: ruleSetActionButtons

Emitted as ONE roster record rather than six fields because the corpus documents them as one selection-scoped toolbar, and splitting them would inflate the field count without adding drivable detail.

fields.name: addRule
fields.label: Add

fields.name: rulesGrid
fields.label: Rules
fields.sourceQuote: Then, as each rule is added using the Add button, they will appear at the bottom of the Rules window in rows.
fields.notes: The Rules tab grid. Existing default rules can be edited in place or removed: 'You can either change a default rule by selecting and updating, or delete the rule by selecting and clicking Delete. Be sure to clear the default rule set if you do not intend to use them.' The shipped default rule set is documented by example as Unit Price and Remit Address. Multiple rules may target the same field (e.g. Shipping by both amount and percentage).

fields.name: matchStatusOutcome

Its 2078-byte sibling match-rules-and-match-status-8cc2c56b.md does NOT carry the catalog. The status is written to the Audit Trail whenever it changes.

fields.name: unlockRuleSet
fields.label: Change to Non-PO

LABEL CONTRADICTION 2:1 - see contradictions. fields.label: Copy

The Level label here uses an EN DASH.

Most clients must map spend to expense types/GL codes or create a Spend Category custom field coded on the invoice or the PO.

Policies is already in the graph - never re-home this field.

Invoice Settings is already in the graph.

Re-runs fire on header save, line item delete/save/sequence change, owner/vendor change or reassignment, PO import that newly matches, and receipt import - regardless of workflow status.
dependencyCandidates.sourceQuote: Rules _cannot_ be run if an invoice:

contradictions.topic: How many tolerance options the Tolerance control offers, and whether Currency is one of them

readings.summary: step-3 enumerates FOUR options as a bullet run - None, Within (+/-), Custom, Currency - with Currency presented as a peer tolerance choice.
readings.sourceQuote: Currency: Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system. This functions as for other rule sets, including audit rules.

readings.summary: configure-three-way-matching enumerates THREE inline - None, Within, Custom - drops the (+/-) suffix, omits Currency entirely, and makes Value/Percentage the immediate next choice.
readings.sourceQuote: If applicable, in the Tolerance section, select None, Within, or Custom, and then select Value or Percentage.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Probe for four options first; if the control offers only three, treat Currency as a downstream refinement of Value rather than a missing option and continue. Never write 'Within (+/-)' as the literal selector without also trying 'Within'. Do not fail a run because Currency is absent at the Line Item - Receipt level.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS, not a finding: the offered list is probably level- or provisioning-dependent, with Currency surfacing only where a currency conversion is meaningful (amount-based rules). configure-three-way is scoped entirely to the Line Item - Receipt level, which may explain the shorter list. The corpus never states a rule, so no reconciliation is possible.

contradictions.topic: How deep the Rules and Life to Date tabs sit under the Purchase Order Matching Rules page

readings.summary: step-3 places the Rules tab ONE level down - straight inside Purchase Order Matching Set, with no Edit Rules step at all.
readings.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab.

readings.summary: step-2 places both tabs TWO levels down: select the rule set and Edit, then select Default and Edit Rules, and only then click the Life to Date tab.
readings.sourceQuote: Select Default, then click Edit Rules (this named rules group is the basis for your new rules group).

readings.summary: configure-three-way-matching agrees with step-2: Edit Rules opens a named rules window, and the Life to Date tab is inside that window.
readings.sourceQuote: Double-click the rule you want to use, and then, in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules. The Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window appears.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Drive the MAJORITY tree (2 topics to 1): page > select rule set > Edit > select rule group > Edit Rules > [Rules | Life to Date]. If no Edit Rules control is present after opening the rule set, fall back to looking for the Rules tab one level up before failing. Note also that the two majority topics disagree on HOW the rule set is opened - Edit button versus double-click.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: step-3 is written as a continuation of step-2 and simply elides the two navigation steps its predecessor already performed, rather than describing a different UI. Cannot be confirmed from the corpus, so the driver must probe both depths.

contradictions.topic: Whether the Level list has three values or four

readings.summary: tools-guides names only three levels - Header, Vendor, Line Item.
readings.sourceQuote: They can be specified at the Header, Vendor, or Line Item level, and can be applied on a one-to-one basis between the current invoice and the PO

readings.summary: admin-guides step-3 names four, adding Line Item - Receipt.
readings.sourceQuote: Select a value from Level (Header, Vendor, Line Item, Line Item - Receipt), so the matching rule operates for the field(s) you want compared.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Expect four; treat a three-value list as a site without three-way matching provisioned rather than as a documentation error, and fail any Line Item - Receipt rule request explicitly with that diagnosis rather than silently substituting Line Item.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: Line Item - Receipt exists only where receipt data (Quantity Receipt Import / Concur Receiving) is in play, so the tools topic - which is a general description of match rules, not a three-way-matching topic - may simply predate or exclude it. Provisioning-dependence is the more likely cause than an error.

contradictions.topic: The label of the Actions-menu command that unlocks an In Use rule set

readings.summary: The New Experience twin writes it 'Change to Non PO Invoice' - no hyphen, with the word Invoice appended.
readings.sourceQuote: it might be feasible to use the Change to Non PO Invoice option in the Actions menu to remove the matching rule set from all relevant invoices

readings.summary: The standalone admin topic writes it 'Change to Non-PO' - hyphenated, no trailing Invoice.
readings.sourceQuote: it might be feasible to use the Change to Non-PO option in the Actions menu to remove the matching rule set from all relevant invoices

readings.summary: A tools-guides procedure breaks the tie in favour of 'Change to Non-PO' and gives the concrete click sequence.
readings.sourceQuote: In the Actions menu, click Change to Non-PO.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Probe 'Change to Non-PO' first (2 attestations to 1, and the only one inside an executable procedure); fall back to 'Change to Non PO Invoice'. Better still, match the Actions-menu item on a case-insensitive substring of 'non' plus 'po' rather than an exact string.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: prose drift in the New Experience republish rather than a genuine relabelling in the new UI - the two admin passages are otherwise word-for-word identical, which is what an editing slip looks like. This directly qualifies the brief's claim that the New Experience twin contributes a unique procedure: the procedure is not unique, only the label differs.

contradictions.topic: How many routes exist for importing the Quantity Receipt file that three-way matching depends on

readings.summary: admin-guides names THREE routes: FTP import, API, or entering receipt data using Concur Receiving.
readings.sourceQuote: they need to import the Quantity Receipt file, which they can do through an FTP import, through the API, or by entering receipt data using Concur Receiving

readings.summary: tools-guides names only TWO - FTP or API - and instead adds a claim about extract availability.
readings.sourceQuote: they need to import the Quantity Receipt file, which they can do through an FTP import or through the API

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not assume manual receipt entry is available. Treat Concur Receiving as a separately activated capability (the roles matrix confirms 'The Concur Receiving feature must be activated' for Central Receiver and Receipt User) and verify it before planning a manual-entry path.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: the tools topic predates the Concur Receiving manual-entry capability, or is scoped to file-interface work only. Distinct loios, so this is a genuine cross-directory divergence, not a republish. Corroborating third source: configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md also names all three routes.

contradictions.topic: How many three-way purchase order matching rules exist and how many a client should use

readings.summary: tools-guides says THREE rules are available but then recommends using 'both' of them, and documents only one of the three by heading.
readings.sourceQuote: With three-way matching, three purchase order matching rules are available. SAP Concur recommends that clients use both these rules to get the most out of this feature.

readings.summary: admin-guides names three specific rules across two tabs and recommends using all three.
readings.sourceQuote: To use three-way matching, the admin can select the Line Item – Receipt rule in the Rules tab and the Matched against Received Quantity rule in the Life to Date tab. SAP Concur recommends that clients use all three of these rules for three-way matching.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Configure all three: on the Rules tab, Level = Line Item - Receipt with the Line Quantity/Received Quantity pairing AND with the Receipt Associated/Receipt Associated pairing; on the Life to Date tab, Match against Received Quantity. Ignore the tools topic's 'both' - it is internally inconsistent with its own sentence.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: the tools sentence was edited from two rules to three without updating 'both'. Note the admin quote is ALSO internally odd - it names two rules in the sentence then says 'all three of these' - so the third is only recoverable from step 3's two Payment Request/Purchase Order pairings. Neither topic lists three headings; the tools topic supplies only 'The Line Item – Receipt: Line Quantity Rule'.

contradictions.topic: How the Life to Date received-quantity rule is spelled

readings.summary: configure-three-way-matching writes it in the past tense, 'Matched against Received Quantity', in its overview bullet - and then writes it WITHOUT the -ed in its own step 8.
readings.sourceQuote: the Matched against Received Quantity rule in the Life to Date tab

readings.summary: The canonical Life to Date selection table writes it 'Match against Received Quantity'.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Match on 'atch against Received Quantity' (substring) rather than an exact label. The table form 'Match against Received Quantity' is the better first probe - it is the one in the authoritative catalog and is also used by the same file's own procedure step.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: prose slip in a summary bullet, not a UI variant - the same file uses both forms, which rules out a per-UI difference.

contradictions.topic: How the fourth Level value is punctuated

readings.summary: configure-three-way-matching uses an EN DASH with spaces.
readings.sourceQuote: In the Level list, select Line Item – Receipt

readings.summary: step-3 uses an ASCII HYPHEN with spaces.
tools-guides uses a hyphen with NO surrounding spaces.
readings.sourceQuote: then the Line Item-Receipt rule will throw an exception

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Never match this option by exact string. Normalise dashes and whitespace before comparing, or match on 'Receipt' scoped to the Level list. A grep -F or an equality test on a retyped dash WILL fail.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: typographic inconsistency across SAP authoring passes, not three different labels. Recorded because it is the single most likely cause of a silent automation miss on this page.

notes: LENS C (tools-guides and cross-cutting). Coverage 'good': 24 fields, 9 value sets, 13 dependencies, 8 contradictions. TOOLS-GUIDES WEIGHT: I exhausted concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/ before opening admin-guides, and 10 of the 26 cited files (38%) are tools-guides - against the 23-of-337 baseline this lens exists to correct. UI VARIANT: I read BOTH twins in full and did NOT claim 'both' on any field. purchase-order-matching-rules-8b357dbb.md and purchase-order-matching-rules-new-experience-6c8fb80f.md are byte-identical through their capability bullet list; the New Experience file then inlines four topics that all exist standalone (test-and-change-match-rule-sets, activate-exchange-rates, before-you-begin) and contributes NO unique control. It does differ on ONE label - 'Change to Non PO Invoice' vs 'Change to Non-PO' - which is emitted as a contradiction, not as a variant, because a tools-guides procedure attests the hyphenated form 2:1 and the surrounding prose is otherwise word-for-word identical, which is what an editing slip looks like rather than a relabelled UI. Every field is therefore 'undifferentiated'. This CONFIRMS-BY-CONTRADICTION the brief's claim (5): the twin's unlock procedure is not unique to it. COULD NOT DETERMINE: (1) the contents of the Payment Request and Purchase Order field lists - the corpus NEVER enumerates them for any Level except Line Item - Receipt, only scattering example members (Unit Price, Shipping, Quantity, Remit Address, Request Total, Custom field) across topics; I left validValues empty rather than assemble a partial list. (2) whether 'Overage Tolerance' is a distinct control or configure-three-way-matching's name for the Life to Date tab's Tolerance section - single attestation, no corroboration. (3) the condition operand catalog for the Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions dialog - step-4 is the only attestation and shows no list; I deliberately did NOT borrow the Audit Rules Condition page catalog (the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md, 288 bullets), which belongs to a different, already-built page. (4) whether the rule set is opened by Edit or by double-click - step-2 says Edit, configure-three-way says double-click, both at the same depth. (5) the cleared state of Allow Submit/Approve - only 'select this check box' is documented, so no Yes/No pair is asserted. NO COMPRESSED RANGES: nothing on this page is written in compressed form ('Custom 01 - 20' style). The only dash-ranges in the corpus for this page are step ranges ('Repeat steps 1-3'), which are not configuration ranges, so compressedRanges is honestly empty rather than padded. TOOLS-GUIDES ROLES MATRIX (required-roles-ef2c2901.md, 6 rows x 4 columns) enumerated here rather than emitted as a value set, because no role-assignment control lives on THIS page: Purchase Order Processor (add/edit/delete receipts and receipt images, in the transmitted purchase order, no conditions); Invoice Processor (same, in the Purchase Order tab of the opened invoice, no conditions); Purchase Request User (same, in the transmitted purchase order, conditional on the Invoice Settings option 'Allow Purchase Request Owners to Edit their own Purchase Orders' or on holding the Receipt User role); Invoice User (same, in the Purchase Order tab of the opened invoice, no conditions); Central Receiver (add/edit/delete receipts for all POs in their group but cannot transmit or process POs or invoices, in the transmitted purchase order, requires Concur Receiving activated); Receipt User (add/edit/delete receipts, own purchase orders only, in the transmitted purchase order, requires Concur Receiving activated). The one control this matrix reaches into is emitted as a dependency on Invoice Settings. MATCH STATUS emitted deliberately as a flagged non-control (matchStatusOutcome) so the complete 6-value catalog is preserved without anyone later mistaking it for a configurable list; the same reasoning applies to unlockRuleSet, which sits on My Invoices but is the only documented way to clear the In Use lock that gates every write here. CORPUS DEFECT ACKNOWLEDGED: create-purchase-order-matching-rules-adb700f9.md is TRUNCATED (body ends on a bare 'x'). I took NOTHING from it as a primary source; it appears only as corroboration in two notes, each flagging the truncation. DUPLICATE CONSTRAINT: general-notes-ced8d7d0.md and not-possible-to-base-rule-set-on-expense-type-or-account-code-e98c9b2c.md publish the same limitation; emitted ONCE, as a dependency on Policies. OWNERSHIP DISCIPLINE: PO Matching Ruleset stays on Policies; Delivery Slip Number and Purchase Order Number stay on Forms and Fields; the data-attribute line association option and the Purchase Request Owner edit option stay on Invoice Settings; Is Purchase Order line Associated / Is Receipt Associated stay on Audit Rules; instructional text stays on Localization (not yet built, dependency legitimately unresolved); exchange rates stay in the Expense Admin module, outside this graph. BEYOND THE INVENTORY: my own tools-guides sweeps (grep -ril 'matching rule' and a UI-variant sweep) surfaced seven further tools files I read - enabling-and-disabling-line-item-level-po-ef3f19cd, resolve-exceptions-09eb0af1, processor-resolve-exceptions-54f71448, associate-po-to-invoice-by-using-capture-processing-dfe82411, po-based-invoices-that-should-not-be-matched-8b4f5ef2, po-association-and-policy-8b4f71b2, matching-summary-tab-a7ac0851. All describe END-USER surfaces (My Invoices, Matching Summary tab, Side-by-Side Editor, Invoice Capture Verification page), so none yielded an admin control and none is emitted. Worth recording as a negative: the UI-variant sweep found NO 'new experience' or 'legacy' file in tools-guides touching PO matching at all, which is why no tools-guides evidence could support a 'both' claim.
